jobs.description:
**Description**
What if you could talk to your Amazon Store? With Alexa+ on Echo Show, customers can now do exactly that. The full Amazon store is live on Echo Show 15 and 21 — a new way to shop at home that combines voice as a natural way to express needs with the product details, reviews, and videos customers rely on to make confident decisions.
  
  
This product started with an ambitious question and was built from scratch — no prior version to iterate on, no existing architecture to extend, no playbook to follow. The team pioneered novel challenges including rendering the full, always-current Amazon store natively on Echo Show in real time, building visual grounding from scratch so Alexa's responses stay anchored to what the customer sees on screen, and creating a conversational commerce paradigm that lets customers skip screens entirely with natural language.
  
  
We are seeking a Software Development Engineer to help build the next chapter of this experience — scaling what we've built, expanding to new surfaces and marketplaces, and pushing the boundaries of agentic, multimodal shopping. As an early-career engineer on this team, you'll design and build meaningful components alongside experienced engineers, own your work through design, implementation, testing, and livesite, and grow quickly in a high-ownership environment.
  
  
This is greenfield, 0→1 work at the intersection of Generative AI, multimodal experiences, and conversational commerce. You will have the freedom to experiment, learn, and invent on behalf of our customers, and you'll work for a strong leadership team that optimizes for your growth and pairs you with mentors who will guide your career.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  
As a Software Development Engineer I on this team, you will:
  
  

* Design, build, test, and operate features that scale and extend the Amazon Store experience on Echo Show and Fire devices.
* Write high-quality, well-tested code and participate actively in code reviews, both giving and receiving thoughtful feedback.
* Contribute to systems that render the Amazon store in real time, keep it in sync, and support conversational, multimodal shopping flows.
* Help extend the experience to new surfaces and international marketplaces, working through ambiguity where there is no existing playbook.
* Own your components end-to-end through livesite operations — monitoring, on-call participation, and continuous improvement of reliability and performance.
* Collaborate with engineering, science, product, and design partners across Alexa Shopping, including teammates in Seattle across time zones.
* Contribute ideas to technical designs, ask good questions, and grow your scope and autonomy over time with support from senior engineers and mentors.

A day in the life
  
  
Here's what a typical day might look like. You'll spend meaningful time building — designing and implementing features that scale the Amazon Store experience on Echo Show and Fire devices, whether that's improving how the store renders in real time, sharpening visual grounding, or extending the experience to a new marketplace. You'll write code, review your teammates', and get thoughtful feedback on yours.
  
  
Days blend focused coding with a short standup, design conversations where your ideas are genuinely wanted, and pairing with a senior engineer or mentor when you're working through something ambiguous. Because this is 0→1 work, you'll often be making decisions without a playbook — and that's the fun part. You'll partner closely with engineering, science, product, and design colleagues across Alexa Shopping, many of them in Seattle, so some collaboration spans time zones.
  
  
Your internal stakeholders are the product, design, and partner engineering teams shaping the Alexa+ shopping experience; your end customers are shoppers at home talking to their Echo Show, expecting it to just work. The problems you'll tackle range from "how do we keep the store always in sync and fast on-device?" to "how do we make a conversational shopping flow feel effortless?" — meaty, customer-facing problems where what you build lands in people's living rooms.
  
  
**About The Team**
We're the team that taught the Amazon Store to talk back. We took an idea that didn't have a blueprint and shipped it to customers' living rooms — and now we're just getting to the fun part: making it bigger, faster, and available to shoppers around the world.
  
  
Our mission is simple to say and hard to do: make shopping on Alexa feel effortless and delightful, no matter where a customer is or which device they reach for. We sit right where voice, vision, and Generative AI meet retail at Amazon scale — which means the problems we solve genuinely haven't been solved before, and the person who cracks them is often the newest engineer with a fresh idea.
  
  
Culture-wise, we're builders who like ambiguity and dislike bureaucracy. We ship, we learn, we tell stories over chai, and we celebrate the wins (and the instructive failures). We hire smart people and give them room to run — you'll own real problems from day one, with experienced engineers and mentors in your corner, not looking over your shoulder. We take the work seriously and ourselves a little less so. If you like the idea of building something customers can literally talk to, you'll fit right in.

* Experience contributing to the architecture and design (architecture, design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and current systems

**Preferred Qualifications**

As an SDE I, you'll join one of two full-stack engineering teams within WEX's Mobility organization.

  
  

Both teams own their systems end to end. The 10-4 (OTR) team builds the over-the-road platform customer-facing APIs, event-driven microservices (Java/Spring Boot, Python), Kafka-based async

processing, payment and identity integrations (Fiserv, Okta), and the Android and iOS apps that drivers use in the field. The NA Mobility Platform team builds and owns the shared frontend infrastructure that product teams across the organization depend on Angular micro-frontends with NestJS BFFs, Module Federation, a shared component library (Theseus UI), brand theming, and app scaffolding via Theseus Builder. In both cases, you'll work across layers of a real production stack, ship to real users, and be supported by engineers who care about doing the work well. We value clean APIs, strong testing habits, and engineers who improve the systems they touch. You'll work closely with the product, other OTR teams, and your peers on features from design through implementation, testing, deployment, and production support.

  
  

**How You'll Make an Impact**

* Build specific components within an established architecture.
* You'll follow the patterns your team has set, whether that's microservices, event-driven design, or component-based frontend, and implement features correctly within those structures rather than redefining them.
* Write clean, compilable code with unit tests that meet the team's quality standards.
* Before you start building, you'll ask the right questions about acceptance criteria and error states so you're solving the right problem, not just writing code.
* Identify and fix bugs in well-defined tasks.
* You'll reproduce issues, pinpoint where in the code they're happening, and work with senior engineers to land the right fix rather than just patching the symptom.
* Handle low-priority support tickets as a first responder and participate in on-call rotations under supervision.
* During incidents, you'll run specific checks and scripts as directed, building your confidence with live systems gradually and safely.
* Contribute to basic observability by adding error and info logging that helps the team debug issues.
* You won't be expected to triage complex production problems alone, but your logs should make it easier for others to do so.
* Keep the team's process running smoothly. That means updating Jira daily, following the
* Definition of Done, moving tickets through the right stages, and raising a flag immediately if something is at risk.
* You don't deviate from the team's agreed process without checking first.
* Show up fully in team rituals like standups, backlog grooming, and demos.
* You'll listen to stakeholder feedback during demos to understand how your work actually lands with users, not just whether it passed the acceptance criteria.
* Use AI tools like Cursor or similar to reduce boilerplate, get unstuck faster, and understand error messages more quickly. You own the quality of everything you ship though, which means validating AI-generated output rather than passing it through unchecked.
* Update documentation when you find something inaccurate or missing. Good documentation is part of the job, and you'll be expected to keep it honest as you learn the system.

jobs.description:
Enterprises want agents that can do real work on their own data. That data sits across documents, databases and business systems that were never built for agents to read, and today's agents forget most of what they learn once a session ends.

Our team builds Sarvam's context engine to solve both problems. The knowledge side brings an enterprise's data together so agents can search it, navigate it and cite where an answer came from. The memory side lets agents remember what they learn over time, about individual users, about teams, and across the organisation. We want both to keep improving as they are used.

Knowledge and memory for agents is a rapidly evolving field. We want to build at the frontier of it, and to show with measurable results that our approach does better than traditional ones.

**About Sarvam**
----------------

Sarvam is India's leading full-stack AI company, building sovereign AI infrastructure and applications purpose-built for India. Headquartered in Bengaluru and founded by leading AI researchers, Sarvam builds foundational models for Indian languages, enterprise AI platforms, and voice-first AI agents that serve hundreds of millions of Indians. Sarvam is backed by top-tier investors and works with national and state governments, large enterprises, and developers across the country. We are building the AI layer for a billion people.

**What this role promises you**
-------------------------------

You will join a small team and own large parts of the platform. The work is driven by real customer deployments, so what you build gets used quickly and you see what works and what does not. You will also work closely with the teams building Sarvam's models, document AI and inference, which makes it much easier to solve problems that cut across the stack.

**What you'll do**
------------------

* Build and run the ingestion pipeline that parses, extracts and indexes large volumes of documents, and keep it reliable when files are messy and external services fail.
* Connect to databases and enterprise systems so agents can work with structured records as well as documents.
* Design how enterprise data is modelled, including the ontology, matching the same entity across sources, and tracing every value back to where it came from.
* Build the retrieval tools agents call, with search, filters and citations, and make them fast and cheap enough for agents to use heavily.
* Build memory for agents at the level of a user, a team and the whole organisation: how it is written, stored, retrieved and kept accurate over time.
* Run evals, find where answers go wrong, and keep iterating until quality improves.
* Work with product and forward-deployed engineers to turn what one customer needs into something the platform does for every customer.
* Write design docs and keep decisions documented.

Our production stack is Go, with Temporal, OpenSearch and Postgres.

**Who you are**
---------------

We are hiring at 3 to 5 years of experience.

* You have built and run backend or data systems in production, and you have fixed them when they broke.
* You are strong in at least one backend language. Our core is in Go, so Go experience is a plus, and you should be happy to work in it every day.
* You have good fundamentals in data modelling and PostgreSQL.
* You have worked on long-running pipelines and know how to make them safe to retry and recover.
* You have worked on search or retrieval and know how to debug why the right result did not come back.
* You use AI coding tools every day and have a good sense of where they help and where they don't.
* You care about measuring quality, and you are comfortable building the evals to do it.

**Bonus points**
----------------

* Experience with knowledge graphs, ontologies, entity resolution or structured extraction.
* Experience building memory for agents or LLM applications.
* Document processing, such as OCR, layout or table extraction.
* Connectors or change data capture for ERP, CRM or other enterprise systems.
* Building on MCP, or serving LLMs and embedding models in production.
* On-prem or air-gapped deployments.
* Experience at an early- or growth-stage startup.

**Job Summary**    

Mission Software Protocol Engineer

Spacecraft | Software | Mission Technology

About the Role

Ever wondered what happens after an operator clicks Send Command in Mission Control. This role sits right in the middle of that journey. We are looking for a recent engineering graduate or a candidate with 1-2 years of relevant experience who is excited to work at the intersection of spacecraft systems, flight software and Mission Control software.

You will help connect the software used to operate the satellite on the ground with the flight software running onboard the spacecraft, making sure commands are correctly built, transmitted and interpreted, and that acknowledgements and telemetry are received and understood.

  
   
  **Responsibilities**    

* Bridge the gap between Mission Technology and spacecraft/flight software teams.
* Understand the flow of telecommands and telemetry from Mission Control to the ground station, satellite and subsystems, and back.
* Work with CCSDS packets and frames, command encoding and decoding, acknowledgements, CRCs and telemetry formats.
* Understand command and telemetry interfaces for EPS, ADCS, OBC/CDH, Payload, Communication and Thermal systems.
* Translate spacecraft and mission requirements into clear software and interface requirements.
* Work with ICDs, command dictionaries, telemetry definitions and communication data flows.
* Test Mission Control-spacecraft interfaces using SIL, FlatSat, simulators and integration environments.
* Debug issues across software, communication protocols and spacecraft interfaces alongside multiple engineering teams.

  
   
  **Bonus Skills**    

* Exposure to any of these will give you an edge: Python, C/C++, Linux, Git, TCP/IP, UDP, APIs, binary and hexadecimal data, packet parsing, embedded systems, software architecture, and SIL/HIL/FlatSat testing.

  
   
  **Why This Role Is Interesting**    

You understand the entire operational chain of a satellite: how a command is created on Earth, reaches a spacecraft in orbit, gets executed by flight software, and comes back as telemetry. If you want to build a career around spacecraft systems, flight software, mission operations and satellite-ground integration, this role gives you exposure to all of them from day one.

  
   
  **Requirements**    

* Recent graduate or engineer with 1-2 years of relevant experience in Aerospace, Aeronautical, Avionics, Electronics or a related field.
* Basic understanding of LEO satellites and spacecraft subsystems.
* Interest in satellite flight software, TTC, Mission Control and Ground Segment systems.
* Familiarity with CCSDS or spacecraft communication protocols is a plus.
* Comfortable understanding technical interfaces, system architecture and data flows.
* Strong curiosity, problem-solving ability and communication skills.

  
   
  **Benefits**    

* Work on real satellite missions - Help define and validate the commands, telemetry and software connections used to operate satellites in orbit.
* Meaningful ownership - Take responsibility for technical definitions, test cases and issue resolution that affect mission readiness.
* Career growth - Develop toward greater technical ownership as the Mission Technology team grows.
* Hands-on learning - Gain experience with CCSDS protocols, flight software, ground stations, FlatSat testing and mission workflows.
* Competitive compensation - Salary aligned with your experience and responsibilities.
* Collaborative team - Work closely with spacecraft, flight software, ground software and mission operations engineers.
